newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. plans $225 mln package for localities.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. plans $225 mln package for localities.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson will propose a $225 million package to aid the state's cash-strapped cities and counties as part his revised 1997-1998 budget plan, his office said on Monday.

The package will include $100 million in property tax relief, $75 million in county hospital funding, and $50 million for the state infrastructure bank to fund local projects, Wilson administration officials said.
Wilson's $225 million plan will be included in his 1997-1998 budget revision, scheduled for release on Wednesday.
The proposal reflects the state's recent economic gains.

According to a report issued last week by the state's legislative analyst, California's economy continues to gather steam, and at this pace could generate $2 billion more in revenues for the state than the governor had projected.

Revenues from the state's three major taxes -- which account for over 93 percent of general fund revenues -- were up $520 million in April, reflecting higher-than-expected final payments on 1996 personal income tax returns.
The April gain brought cumulative 1996-1997 revenues to $825 million above Wilson's January budget estimate, the legislative analyst said.
At this rate, the legislative analyst said revenues over the current year and the next budget year combined would exceed the governor's January budget estimate by $2 billion.
